periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption finished 2024-Q3 at 65.7%, comfortably above the >=60% target and establishing the baseline for this reporting arc. Since this is our first quarter in the sequence, there is no prior-quarter movement to report, but the starting point is strong and council-ready. The cleanest gains came from HarborConnect utility payments, online Parks class registration, and Accela permit intake for small residential remodels, where the counter teams used the same scripts and QR cards at City Hall. Data quality looks solid: IT and Customer Experience reconciled portal counts against cashiering batches before close, which keeps departments looking as good as the work they are doing.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the Friday noon department sign-off cycle for HarborConnect, Accela, and Parks so the adoption number stays audit-ready. Extend the QR-card pilot to the Marina Office and the senior center front desk before the next billing wave. Ask each high-volume counter to identify one transaction that can be nudged online without reducing walk-in service quality.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption remained at 65.7% in 2024-Q4, a quarter-over-quarter movement of 0.0 percentage points from 2024-Q3 and still 5.7 points above the >=60% target. Holding steady through holiday staffing, storm-season call volume, and year-end permit rush is a good operating signal, not a stall. The Development Services team kept online submittals stable by assigning two permit techs to the B-12 commercial tenant-improvement queue, while Finance saw consistent autopay enrollment during the December utility cycle. From a scorecard perspective, the number is green and dependable, and the supporting department notes were submitted on time.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current level by preserving the year-end cross-training playbook for utility billing, permits, and service requests. Extend adoption by adding a one-click HarborConnect link to the printed January utility insert and the business license renewal email. Watch the B-12 permit queue in the first two weeks of 2025 so any online intake friction is fixed before the spring construction ramp.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption increased to 67.8% in 2025-Q1, up 2.1 percentage points quarter over quarter from 65.7% in 2024-Q4 and still green against the >=60% target. This is the kind of measured lift we want: visible, explainable, and backed by operations rather than one-time promotion. The January HarborConnect refresh, the Library card-renewal workflow, and Code Compliance service requests on Route C-4 all contributed to residents choosing digital first. Departments also improved the denominator review, with IT flagging duplicate guest checkouts before the ClearPoint update window closed.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by keeping the monthly data-quality huddle on the second Tuesday, with IT, Finance, Development Services, Library, and Customer Experience all present. Extend the Q1 gains by moving the top 10 Code Compliance request types into guided online forms with plain-language prompts. For council reporting, package this as a workforce capacity story: more digital intake means staff spend more time resolving cases and less time re-keying forms.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption reached 69.6% in 2025-Q2, up another 1.8 percentage points from 67.8% in 2025-Q1 and well above the >=60% target. The chronological story is now clear: after the 2024 plateau, we have two consecutive quarters of meaningful growth. Summer recreation enrollment, beach parking permit renewals, and online inspection scheduling for the Seabreeze and Alder subdivisions gave residents several practical reasons to use digital channels. I appreciate that departments reported the lift with transaction-level notes, because that makes the green status easy to defend and easy to repeat.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by documenting the Parks and beach parking campaign calendar as a reusable seasonal playbook. Extend adoption by placing HarborConnect ambassadors at the first two Saturday farmers markets in July with tablets for account setup, not just flyers. Keep a watch item on inspection scheduling capacity so online demand does not outpace available inspector slots during peak construction weeks.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption edged up to 69.8% in 2025-Q3, a 0.2 percentage point increase from 69.6% in 2025-Q2 and still firmly green against the >=60% target. The smaller movement is understandable after the strong Q1 and Q2 gains; the program is entering optimization territory rather than launch territory. Customer Experience reported that most remaining in-person volume is concentrated in complex utility move-ins, over-the-counter coastal permits, and residents who need language or accessibility support. The good news is that the September scorecard close was clean, with departments submitting notes before deadline and no late reconciliation issues.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by keeping the existing digital workflows stable through the fall release freeze, especially utility billing and inspection scheduling. Extend adoption by creating assisted-digital appointments for complex utility move-ins, where staff complete the transaction with the resident in HarborConnect rather than outside it. Add Spanish and Vietnamese quick-start cards at City Hall, the Pier kiosk, and the North Harbor library branch to address the remaining access gap respectfully.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption moved to 67.7% in 2025-Q4, down 2.1 percentage points from 69.8% in 2025-Q3 but still green and 7.7 points above the >=60% target. I do not want us to overreact to a green quarter, but I do want us to name the dip plainly. The decrease appears tied to the November HarborConnect authentication update, higher in-person utility assistance during king-tide outreach, and temporary routing of short-term rental renewals through staff review. Departments handled the variance responsibly by documenting the operational causes before the council packet deadline, which is exactly the discipline this scorecard needs.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the authentication update in place but adding a clearer reset-password path and front-desk talking points. Extend adoption by returning short-term rental renewals to a fully digital workflow once the Planning review checklist is embedded in Accela. Track weekly HarborConnect login failures through January so we can tell whether the Q4 decline was a transition effect or a usability issue needing redesign.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption rebounded to 71.2% in 2026-Q1, up 3.5 percentage points from 67.7% in 2025-Q4 and the highest result so far in this sequence. That rebound tells me the Q4 dip was actively managed, not accepted as the new normal. IT’s password-reset fix, the Customer Experience call-back cohort for 1,200 utility customers, and the restored short-term rental renewal workflow all helped move residents back into digital channels. This is a strong green result for the workforce objective because it reduces manual intake pressure while preserving service access for people who still need help.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 71.2% level by locking the Q1 fixes into standard operating procedures, including the password-reset script and the short-term rental digital checklist. Extend adoption by adding digital completion coaching to new-employee onboarding for front-counter staff, so every department nudges residents the same way. Prepare a concise council slide showing the Q4-to-Q1 recovery, because the quarter-over-quarter increase is a useful proof point for disciplined management.

periods.analysis: Digital Service Adoption improved again to 71.6% in 2026-Q2, up 0.4 percentage points from 71.2% in 2026-Q1 and continuing well above the >=60% target. The pace is modest, but at this adoption level modest growth is a healthy signal of sustained performance rather than campaign noise. Beach parking renewals, online bulky-item pickup scheduling on sanitation Routes 2 and 5, and the new mobile-friendly business license amendment form all supported the gain. Across the full arc, Harborview moved from 65.7% in 2024-Q3 to 71.6% in 2026-Q2, and the departments have given us a credible, data-clean story to put in front of council.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping quarterly transaction audits in place and publishing a simple department-by-department adoption dashboard before each reporting deadline. Extend adoption by targeting the remaining high-volume paper processes: utility move-out forms, encroachment permit supplements, and senior recreation scholarship renewals. Set a practical next operating milestone of maintaining adoption above 70% for two more quarters while protecting assisted access for residents who need it.

periods.analysis: Digital adoption increased to 50.3% but missed its 55% target. The workforce retention plan is also at 65% with several overdue inputs, even though online permitting went live.
periods.recommendations: Assign the remaining retention reviews and measure adoption after launch rather than counting launch as uptake.
